record_reviews.summary: Hooker reports that his aunt could not obtain Oxford lodgings and relays the Jacobson alternative; he gives a structural diagnosis of Darwin’s “monstrous flower,” then reports Van Diemen’s Land/New Zealand collections and rejects migration as sufficient for their shared alpine flora pending tabulation.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Exact 16 June 1847; the within-letter sequence separates lodging (P1), flower (P2), and Hooker’s own collections/theory (P3).

evidence.quote: I only received my Aunts letter this afternoon in time to post it on to you I am very sorry to find by its contents that she could not procure the lodgings you wished.
Many thanks for your kindness about the lodgings—it will be of great use to me.
Your monstrous flower of Cytisus has the stamens all right but one of the 2 parts of the keel has got inside the staminal column
I enclose a flower with apparently a single stamen having become foliaceous & bilateral—

record_reviews.summary: Darwin apologizes for burdening Mrs Jacobson, accepts Magdalen Hall rooms with private meals, gives arrival instructions, declines Daubeny’s party, and explains his preference for Oxford arrangements.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Exact 17 June 1847; the body follows Hooker’s 16 June lodging report.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Darwin’s four paragraphs are complete.

evidence.quote: The Magdalen Hall rooms will do capitally

record_reviews.summary: Darwin acknowledges safe arrival of Hooker’s books but notes the missing October 1845 Phytologist, promises to return the loan, and reacts to Hooker’s Van Diemen’s Land/New Zealand plants by asking Hooker to mark plants common or analogous across the southern floras.
